piece_type: DTC TV ad with celebrity spokesperson

cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: Serena Williams VO: “With Ubrelvy, there’s another option. One dose works fast to eliminate migraine pain.” | SUPER: “UBRELVY® QUICKLY ELIMINATES MIGRAINE PAIN” | Serena Williams VO: “Migraine pain relief starts with U. Ask about Ubrelvy.”
cases.context: Before/after visuals (photophobia, then relaxed on blue path); celebrity amplifies credibility; small SUPER 'Some people had pain freedom within 2 hours' does not mitigate. Prior advisory comments March 10, 2020.
cases.rationale: Only ~19-22% achieved pain freedom at 2 hours (7.4-9.4% over placebo); claims imply fast, complete elimination for all.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'eliminate(s)', 'quickly', 'fast' combined with symptom/pain claims; require comparison to label responder rates and time point.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “One dose works fast to eliminate migraine pain”
cases.context: 78-81% did not achieve pain freedom after one dose; label permits second dose after 2 hours.
cases.rationale: Implies all patients will be pain-free after a single dose.
cases.check: Does a 'one dose' claim imply universal response when most patients did not respond or may need re-dosing?
